main_issue: The guideline accurately captures XXE caused by unconstrained external XML resource resolution, but the assigned set includes cases with only patch-window metadata or different XML-adjacent mechanisms (for example XSLT behavior, XPath/SSRF, or template-expression injection) without evidence that external entities or DTD/schema/style-sheet resolution is the vulnerable sink.
suggested_guideline: Trace attacker-controlled XML, SOAP, or XML report/configuration input into the exact DocumentBuilderFactory, SAXParserFactory, XMLInputFactory, SchemaFactory, TransformerFactory, or SOAP parser instance that consumes it. Report a finding when that instance can process a DOCTYPE or resolve an external general entity, parameter entity, schema, or stylesheet without a prior restrictive configuration. Verify that the parsed content is attacker-influenced and that protections are applied to the same parser or transformer instance before parse or transform. Remediate by disallowing DOCTYPE where feasible, disabling external general and parameter entities, disabling external DTD loading, setting external-access properties to empty or an allowlist, and installing a rejecting resolver when the API supports one.
split_suggestions: XXE through unconstrained XML parser DTD or external-entity resolution
External resource access through XSLT, schema, XPath, namespace, or SOAP-specific XML processing
Other XML-adjacent vulnerabilities such as XMLDecoder deserialization, interpolation/property disclosure, and parser resource-exhaustion handling
evidence_notes: Allure JUnit/XUnit provides direct source-backed evidence: default DocumentBuilderFactory/DocumentBuilder parses XML files without an external-entity restriction or rejecting resolver.

Bonita, DBeaver, aXMLRPC, and java-xmlbuilder have CWE-611 labels and parser-related patch hunks, which are consistent with the core mechanism, but the supplied payload does not expose enough source detail to confirm the exact external-resolution sink for each.
Fediz has only CWE-20 and patch-hunk anchors; no trace evidence establishes that its flaw is external entity, DTD, schema, or stylesheet resolution.

AWS Android is labeled SSRF and explicitly described only as review-entry retrieval ground truth, not exploit proof; it should not substantiate this mechanism without source evidence of XML external-resource fetching.

HtmlUnit is labeled template_expression_injection and has only a review-entry window. XSLT can be relevant when external stylesheet/document resolution is enabled, but that property is not established here.
The cluster summary itself names several distinct mechanisms beyond XXE, confirming that the group should be partitioned before it is treated as a reusable mechanism set.
